questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Even though languages usually aren't a problem, I knew that choosing France would be a helping hand, as I am already fluent in French. The quality and reputation of Sorbonne University was also something that I had in mind as it not only was a personal challenge to attend and learn with some of the best students in France at Sorbonne, but the program and courses that I could take in Sorbonne were also perfect for my personal developement.
Hence why I chose Sorbonne University.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was sent by mail so there was no problem there, the first day where all erasmus meet is also a benediction as you get to socialise and gather information so I highly encourage this practice to continue!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Any assistance was available on contact with the coordinators, I had a meeting with my coordinators and other Erasmus staff to make sure I had all the documents and information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in a studio owned by my parents. If I can recommend anything for future Erasmus students it would be the residences (for example the one near Reuilly-Diderot)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus comes with rer or metro travel time wich in paris can easilly amount to 30-45min if you live in Paris (intra-muros) and 1h-1h30 if you live on the outsides of paris so travel time is definetly something to lookout for.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the main site of KU you can find the form to apply, after a brief exchange of mails you apply via Mobility-Online, get your OLA and the pre-aproval and finally you are good to go!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinators where there to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesfull, I managed to get all of the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to have all the papers and all the certifications you need very well kept and be tidy about the paperwork

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were on a very high level but it was manageable and accessible for anyone (any academic student)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The french learning system is very different from the danish one, but since i was raised in the french system, i didn't have trouble with the change.

The french system is all about the theory and learning every detail by heart whereas the danish system is all about teamwork, hands-on experience and less about learning every detail, with a special focus on being able to understand and explain the subject.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Physiology, Neurology, Maths, Ecology and Evolution, Biochemistry, Genetics, Animal Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course that i liked the most was Physiology as the balance between hands on and theory was very good and I learned a lot from the course. It is a very hard course though.

questions.answer: I think I had done my research well so I was aware of all the costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general france is less expensive than denmark, I found that electricty bills could be quite extensive, but since it is winter, it might be why it was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports were available and the erasmus community where always trying to go to a club or other activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: sports on campus (fencing, cheer, karate, judo etc..)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: visiting france is always a good idea, in paris, museums, sights as trocadero, the eiffel tower, le marais, etoile and le 15ème in general are always worth going to

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As i was born and raised in Paris, it was very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participating in the erasmus events are very helpful!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the fact that people are less open at first changes from denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Parisian coffee culture is a must try for newcomers

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be afraid to ask people and get to know them!
Explore the city/country you are in!
Enjoy the french culture and make sure you get the most out of the stay, whilst studying

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it is important for the student to get contact with people and join all the whatsapp groups

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finishing the term was very rewarding

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: mid term exams where very stressfull as you have to find the level of where the exam level is

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
